# C62 fixed-query answers: Balance Control v1 POST /balanceTransfer

## Q1

The 2026-09-15 reference at https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/BalanceControlv1/latest/post/balanceTransfer describes Balance Control **v1** `POST /balanceTransfer` as starting a balance-transfer request between **merchant accounts**, on the listed TEST server `https://pal-test.adyen.com/pal/servlet/BalanceControl/v1`. The page does not name a caller role or credential and has no device or session identity. `fromMerchant` and `toMerchant` identify source and destination merchant accounts; those accounts must be under the same company account and legal entity and share at least one processing currency, and the source must have sufficient funds. The body requires `amount.currency` (three-character ISO code) and integer `amount.value` in minor units, both merchant IDs, and a `type` from `tax`, `fee`, `terminalSale`, `credit`, `debit`, and `adjustment`. Optional `reference` has an 80-character maximum and is generated uniquely by Adyen if omitted; optional `description` has a recommended 140-character maximum because it may be truncated. Repeated requests for the same merchant pair must be sequential because parallel requests may not be processed. The page provides no reversal operation, retry/idempotency rule, or completion timing. [[source-adyen-api-explorer-balancecontrolv1-latest-post-balancetransfer]] (raw lines 5–32).

## Q2

The same contract's `200 Success` text says **the request succeeded**, and the response requires a `createdAt` date for when the transfer was **requested**, a 16-character `pspReference`, amount, merchant IDs, type, and `status`. That status can be `transferred`, `failed`, `error`, or `notEnoughBalance`; HTTP 200, request creation time, and the reference do not by themselves establish a successful movement of funds. The example shows `transferred`, but the schema explicitly permits failure states. The page describes no authentication/security role, idempotency or correlation guarantee beyond returned/request references, asynchronous notification or polling outcome, version migration/deprecation, settlement or payout process, or bank receipt. It is Balance Control **v1** merchant-account movement, not evidence for Balance Control v2 or Adyen for Platforms balance-account transfers. https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/BalanceControlv1/latest/post/balanceTransfer; [[source-adyen-api-explorer-balancecontrolv1-latest-post-balancetransfer]] (raw lines 17–18, 25–32, 49–89).

# C62 fixed-query answers: SoftPOS POST /auth/certificate

## Q1

The 2026-09-15 SoftPOS configuration API **v3** reference at https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/softpos-configuration-api/latest/post/auth/certificate describes `POST /auth/certificate` creating a communication session through mutual authentication between the **Mobile SDK** and Adyen payments platform. The request sends an SDK/device-identifying `setupToken` and a required `merchantAccount`; the page lists SDK callback routes for Android and iOS but does not name a separate caller application or transaction session in the request. Its listed servers include TEST and distinct Australia, Asia Pacific South East, Europe, North East Asia and US live regions. Optional `store` must be omitted when merchant accounts act as stores or for a registered payment facilitator. `subMerchantData`, though marked optional in the table, is required for a registered facilitator and prohibited otherwise; its `displayName`, `id`, `mcc` and `name` are required when supplied, with Amex email/phone and Brazil/Cartes Bancaires tax-ID conditions. A successful 201 response can list optional communication-session `id`, SDK `installationId`, merchant/store, and `sdkData`; if the backend creates a Terminal API transaction request, `installationId` is its `MessageHeader.POIID`. Errors are 400, 401, 422 and 500. The page gives no session expiry, renewal, reversal or payment timing rule. [[source-adyen-api-explorer-softpos-configuration-api-latest-post-auth-certificate]] (raw lines 5–55, 67–79, 82–155).

## Q2

The captured 201 response says the **session request succeeded** and provides possible session/installation identity and `sdkData` to pass to the POS app for authenticating Adyen-platform responses. It is not a Terminal API payment response and proves no authorization, capture, reconciliation, settlement or bank receipt. The header schema marks `X-API-Key` **No** while calling it an API-request authentication key; the explicit 401 “Authentication required” prevents interpreting that table flag as permission for unauthenticated use. The introduction refers to a returned “session token,” but the response schema has no field of that name; it lists optional `id` and `sdkData`. The page does not specify an asynchronous callback or correlation contract, session lifetime, retry/deprecation rule, or successful SDK/device attestation beyond this described mutual-authentication request. The 201 and error examples are placeholders, not actual operational outcomes. https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/softpos-configuration-api/latest/post/auth/certificate; [[source-adyen-api-explorer-softpos-configuration-api-latest-post-auth-certificate]] (raw lines 7–34, 67–79, 82–218).

# C62 fixed-query answers: POST /diagnosis

## Q1

The 2026-09-15 capture at https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/terminal-api/latest/post/diagnosis describes a Sale-to-POI Terminal API `POST /diagnosis` request conveying information about the target POI. It lists two cloud **test** device transport URLs, `/v1/merchants/{merchantAccount}/devices/{deviceId}/sync` and `/async`, plus a local-terminal-IP option. Those path segments identify merchant and device routing in the listed cloud transport; the request table separately describes `POIID` as a POI system or terminal identifier referring to `MessageHeader.POIID`. The captured page does not specify the caller's identity, a session ID, or a numbered Terminal API protocol version; `latest` is the API Explorer path and `v1` appears in the cloud device URLs. The request table marks `POIID`, boolean `HostDiagnosisFlag`, and integer-array `AcquirerID` as **not required**; `AcquirerID` is present for a diagnosis limited to those hosts. For the response, `Response` and nested `Result` are required, `POIStatus` and `HostStatus` are optional, and `GlobalStatus` is required only within a supplied `POIStatus` object while `AcquirerID` is required within a supplied host-status object. The page states no default, numeric limit, lifecycle, reversal, or timing rule. [[source-adyen-api-explorer-terminal-api-latest-post-diagnosis]] (raw lines 5–28, 30–53).

## Q2

The same captured contract labels the HTTP response `200 Success`, but its required `Response.Result` may be `Success`, `Failure`, or `Partial`; `ErrorCondition` is absent or unused for Success and must be present in other cases. Optional `AdditionalResponse` is processing information for logging without real-time involvement. Optional `POIStatus` and `HostStatus` report terminal-component availability and host state/reachability; neither HTTP 200 nor those diagnostic fields proves payment authorization, capture, reconciliation, settlement, bank receipt, or any created resource. The captured page provides no authentication/security procedure, request-correlation contract, asynchronous completion rule, deprecation notice, rate limit, retry or reversal rule, or numbered Terminal API protocol version. It lists a cloud `/async` server, but does not define asynchronous outcome delivery or correlation. The separately linked diagnosis guide supplies additional operational behavior, which must retain its own attribution. https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/terminal-api/latest/post/diagnosis; [[source-adyen-api-explorer-terminal-api-latest-post-diagnosis]] (raw lines 10–19, 30–53).

# C62 fixed-query answers: POST /reversal

## Q1

The 2026-09-15 capture at https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/terminal-api/latest/post/reversal describes a Terminal API `POST /reversal` request concerning a **previous payment or loyalty transaction**. It lists cloud **test** `/v1/merchants/{merchantAccount}/devices/{deviceId}/sync` and `/async` URLs and a local-terminal-IP option; the cloud path supplies merchant/device routing, while the request's `OriginalPOITransaction` can separately include a Sale-system `SaleID`, terminal `POIID` if the original transaction came from another POI, and original POI/host identifiers. The page does not state a caller credential, a session ID, or a numbered Terminal API protocol version: `latest` is its Explorer path, `v1` is in the cloud device URL, and the field descriptions refer to the NEXO Sale-to-POI protocol. `OriginalPOITransaction` and `ReversalReason` are required request fields; the reason is one of `CustCancel`, `MerchantCancel`, `Malfunction`, or `Unable2Compl`. The original object's `POITransactionID` and `HostTransactionID` are each marked optional, but each supplied ID object requires its own `TransactionID` and `TimeStamp`. Optional `SaleData` requires `SaleTransactionID` only if that parent is supplied, again with its nested ID and timestamp required. `ReversedAmount` is optional and defaults implicitly to `AuthorizedAmount` when absent. The page specifies no currency requirement, amount cap, reversal completion time, retry window, or subsequent lifecycle. [[source-adyen-api-explorer-terminal-api-latest-post-reversal]] (raw lines 5–19, 21–57).

## Q2

The same captured contract labels its response `200 Success`, yet the required body `Response.Result` permits `Success`, `Failure`, or `Partial`; `ErrorCondition` is absent or unused on Success and required in other cases. Its `POIData`, original-transaction echo, copied reversed amount, and `PaymentReceipt` are optional; `POITransactionID` is required only within a supplied `POIData`, and the optional `POIReconciliationID` identifies a Sale–POI reconciliation period when Result is Success. Thus HTTP 200 alone does not prove a successful reversal, and neither a response receipt nor a reconciliation-period ID proves financial settlement or bank receipt. The API Explorer page does not establish authentication/security procedure, callback correlation, async outcome delivery despite listing an `/async` transport URL, deprecation/version migration, or timing/eligibility guarantees. Separately, the captured referenced POS refund guide says `ReversalResponse.Result: Success` acknowledges a refund request and the later `CANCEL_OR_REFUND` webhook gives the outcome; that is guide evidence, not an additional rule stated in this API Explorer table. https://docs.adyen.com/api-explorer/terminal-api/latest/post/reversal; [[source-adyen-api-explorer-terminal-api-latest-post-reversal]] (raw lines 10–19, 59–100).
